subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should browser `/navigate` and `/act` return the stale acted-on target ID when the backend cannot prove continuity, requiring callers to re-list and explicitly select a target rather than inferring a replacement?
rationale: This is a deliberate user-visible compatibility change in route recovery behavior; source and live evidence support its safety goal, but only the browser contract owner can choose between stale-ID fail-safe semantics and a different supported recovery API.

options.title: Accept stale-ID fail-safe
options.body: Adopt backend-owned outcomes and require callers to re-select whenever continuity cannot be proved, preventing an unrelated tab from being silently adopted.

options.title: Require a different recovery contract
options.body: Define and implement an explicit error or stable backend identity mechanism before merge if stale IDs are not acceptable to existing callers.

recommendation.title: Accept stale-ID fail-safe
recommendation.body: Adopt backend-owned outcomes and require callers to re-select whenever continuity cannot be proved, preventing an unrelated tab from being silently adopted.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report defines the browser target-continuity contract and explicitly requests this acceptance decision.
